system.name: Off-path SmartNIC (Bluefield-2) characterization
system.one_liner: a comparison of RDMA-capable NIC, on-path SmartNIC and off-path SmartNIC hardware architectures and their communication paths

components.name: Client Requests
components.role: requests arriving from RDMA-capable client machines

components.name: NIC cores
components.role: network interface processing cores common to all three architectures

components.name: DRAM
components.role: on-board memory reachable directly by the on-path SmartNIC's offloaded code

components.name: PCIe
components.role: PCIe link connecting NIC cores to host DRAM

components.name: Host DRAM
components.role: host machine's memory, target of RDMA/DMA requests

components.name: PCIe switch
components.role: integrated switch dispatching packets among NIC cores, SoC and host in the off-path design

components.name: SoC cores
components.role: separate general-purpose compute cores (ARM) with their own DRAM, off the network critical path

flows.what: inline requests interacting directly with offloaded code
SoC<->Host communication via RNIC (RDMA) or DMA (DOCA)

content.key_idea: Off-path SmartNICs (like Bluefield-2) add a separate SoC with its own cores, memory and network interface behind a PCIe switch, decoupling offloaded compute from the network critical path unlike on-path SmartNICs, at the cost of longer communication paths through the switch.
content.reading_order: left to right across three side-by-side subfigures (a) RNIC, (b) on-path SmartNIC, (c) off-path SmartNIC, each showing client requests entering NIC cores and reaching host DRAM via PCIe, with (c) adding the SoC and PCIe switch.

summary: This figure compares three NIC hardware architectures relevant to accelerating distributed systems: (a) a plain RDMA-capable NIC (RNIC), where NIC cores use PCIe DMA to access host DRAM; (b) an on-path SmartNIC, where offloaded code sits directly on the critical network path and can access on-board DRAM but competes with host-bound traffic for NIC cores; and (c) an off-path SmartNIC (the paper's focus, exemplified by Bluefield-2), which adds a separate SoC with its own ARM cores and DRAM behind a PCIe switch, keeping offloaded computation off the network's critical path at the cost of extra hops through the switch. Numbered circled labels (①-④) mark the distinct communication paths — client-to-host, client-to-SoC, SoC-to-host (via RNIC or DMA), and SoC offloading — that the paper characterizes experimentally. The three subfigures are drawn as parallel boxed diagrams using a flat, rounded-corner style with color coding (blue NIC cores, orange host DRAM, green SoC, red PCIe switch/bottleneck).
summary_zh: 图1对比三种网卡架构：(a) 普通RDMA网卡(RNIC)通过PCIe DMA访问主机内存；(b) 在路径上的SmartNIC，卸载代码直接位于网络关键路径上；(c) 离路径SmartNIC(如Bluefield-2)，通过PCIe交换机连接独立的SoC核心与内存，使卸载计算脱离网络关键路径，图中以带圈数字标出①-④几类通信路径。
